text:
Vince Dunn plays more than 23 minutes a night for Seattle and leads the Kraken blue line in the usual offensive ways: ten points, four on the power play, 34 shots. He scored late against the Rangers on Nov. 7, his first goal in ten games.

The 5v5 picture is rough. With Dunn on the ice the Kraken have 40% of shot attempts and 44% of expected goals. Evolving-Hockey notes he plays with some of the weakest teammates in the league by impact, which drags those numbers down, but they still had him barely above replacement last season.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains part of it. He gets to dangerous ice for a defenseman (96th percentile for chances from the home-plate area) but only 31% of his zone exits keep possession, so a lot of shifts end with the puck going back the other way.

Off the ice, the story is his contract: KJR and others are asking how close Seattle is to an extension, and where Simon Edvinsson fits. His last ten games produced four points on 6.6 expected, so the offense should tick up.
headline: Dunn's minutes keep coming, the chances keep going the other way
